title: How does the persistence time of a specialist Lenia predator scale with arena size, and does it diverge above a critical size (a law for C:ecology-with-reproduction)?
summary: In 20261026T0003-c26-lenia-predator-arena the R+ predator (building only from MIRd+ prey matter) dies ~100 t after introduction at 160^2, after 710-940 t at 256^2, and is alive at the end (>1200 t) at 320^2 (2 seeds each). Spatial predator-prey theory predicts persistence time growing exponentially with area (or diverging above a critical size). Measuring it gives a falsifiable law with a held-out size.
experiment: world.py of 20261026T0003-c26-lenia-predator-arena with WORLD_P {"PRED":1,"T_INTRO":200,"PSIG":8,"DECB":0.002,"DOMAIN":L}. Run L = 192, 224, 256, 288 with 4 seeds each to t=1600 (192^2 about 8 min, 288^2 about 30 min; split across agents), record the last time with >= 1 predator cell (runle.py), fit log(persistence) against L^2 on three sizes and predict the fourth before running it. Report the prey-predator oscillation period from the counts (peak spacing over >= 3 seeds, as RUBRIC L5 asks). Bonus: a 160^2 run with a predator yield of 0.5 or predator decay 0.001 to see whether the critical size moves.
